title: Constant-scalar and intrinsic constant-ring pullback have the same normalized adjunction
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be small sites in the coefficient universe [def-weil-size-convention], and let $u:\mathcal C	o\mathcal D$ induce a geometric morphism $
u:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)	o\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$: an adjunction $
u^{-1}\dashv
u_*$ with finite-limit-preserving inverse image, whose direct image is $(
u_*N)(U)=N(uU)$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Fix a commutative ring $B$ in the coefficient universe [def-weil-size-convention], possibly zero, and the constant ring sheaves $B_{\mathcal C},B_{\mathcal D}$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Let $\phi:B_{\mathcal C}	o
u_*B_{\mathcal D}$ be the canonical ring-sheaf map sending every constant scalar $b$ to the same constant scalar. Use intrinsic module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $L$ be intrinsic module pullback: apply $
u^{-1}$ to a module and its scalar action, then extend scalars through the canonical constant-ring isomorphism $
u^{-1}B_{\mathcal C}\cong B_{\mathcal D}$; equip $L$ with its module adjunction unit $\eta$ [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image]. Let $L^{\mathrm{sc}},R^{\mathrm{sc}}$ be the module functors obtained by applying the set-sheaf adjunction to addition, zero, negation and every scalar endomorphism $b$, then extending constant scalar actions to the sheafified constant rings, with their transported adjunction and unit $\eta^{\mathrm{sc}}$ [lem-pe-constant-left-module-transport]. Let $R$ be intrinsic module direct image along $\phi$: its sections are $N(uU)$, with scalar restriction through $\phi_U$.
The canonical identifications of underlying section groups give a natural module isomorphism $ho:R^{\mathrm{sc}}\xrightarrow{\sim}R$, whose components are the identity on every section group. Through $ho$, the transported adjunction is $L^{\mathrm{sc}}\dashv R$ with unit $\eta'_M=ho_{L^{\mathrm{sc}}M}\eta^{\mathrm{sc}}_M$. There is a unique natural isomorphism $a:L\xrightarrow{\sim}L^{\mathrm{sc}}$ with
$$R(a_M)\eta_M=\eta'_M$$
for every intrinsic $B_{\mathcal C}$-module $M$. Its inverse $b:L^{\mathrm{sc}}\xrightarrow{\sim}L$ satisfies $R(b_M)\eta'_M=\eta_M$, $b_Ma_M=1_{LM}$ and $a_Mb_M=1_{L^{\mathrm{sc}}M}$. Both inverse-image functors are exact; applying $a$ termwise induces a natural isomorphism between their ordinary derived functors and their bounded-below restrictions [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories], compatible with derived localization.

proof.text: Restrict along the constant ring sheafification unit. Local surjectivity makes restriction fully faithful. Lift multiplication by each constant scalar to an intrinsic module endomorphism: the restricted map is linear because B is commutative. The lift scalar_compatibility field identifies its inverse image. Applying the module adjunction Hom bijection and counit naturality then identifies its direct image with the same scalar endomorphism.

proof.text: Compose directUnderlyingIso and abelianDirectSetIso to obtain the specified natural isomorphism of underlying set sheaves. Both module direct images are right adjoints and preserve finite limits. Section evaluation preserves finite limits; the module category is additive with finite biproducts. Fullness of the forgetful equivalence of left exact functor categories therefore lifts each section comparison to an additive map. Faithfulness proves restriction naturality.

proof.text: The sheafification Hom equivalence evaluated on the definition of constantSectionRingMap proves that it sends each constant scalar to the same scalar at uF(T). Naturality of the section comparison at the scalar endomorphisms from step 1 gives constant-scalar linearity. Fullness of scalar restriction lifts the comparison to a module map retaining its component functions. Sectionwise bijectivity gives an isomorphism, and naturality follows from the additive section transformations.

proof.text: Transport moduleAdj through rho using ofNatIsoRight. Its unit is definitionally the displayed composite. Compare it to the intrinsic pullback-pushforward adjunction with leftAdjointUniq. Its unit formula is exactly unit_equation. Injectivity of the intrinsic Hom bijection proves uniqueness. Compose with the direct image of the inverse comparison and use functoriality and the iso identities to obtain inverse_unit; the other inverse identities are those of the iso.

proof.text: The three exactness properties for the scalar inverse image are fields of the supplied lift. Transport them to the intrinsic inverse image across the inverse comparison using additive_of_iso and preservesFiniteLimits/Colimits_of_natIso.

proof.text: Use Functor.mapDerivedCategoryNatIso and mapDerivedCategoryPlusNatIso on the comparison. mapDerivedCategoryNatIso_fac gives the complex localization square; the inclusion formula together with the identity inclusion comparisons gives the inclusion square; mapDerivedCategoryPlusNatIso_hom_app_factorsh gives the bounded homotopy localization square. The existing bounded construction is the restriction along the full inclusion, preserving the unit route.
